title: Which failures double robustness covers
question: Does a doubly robust MAIC protect against an omitted confounder, and what happens to a sensitivity grid built on a misspecified outcome model?
design: Unanchored transport with a nonlinear outcome, misspecifiable weighting and outcome models and an omitted binary confounder; MAIC, outcome regression and augmented estimators under every combination of model correctness; 16 cells crossing omitted-variable strength, imbalance and overlap. 2000 replicates per cell.
answer: Double robustness protects against one misspecified nuisance model and nothing else. With an omitted confounder the augmented estimator carried exactly the same bias as correctly specified weighting or outcome-regression estimators, and with both models wrong the misspecification and omitted-variable biases added. A sensitivity grid built on a misspecified analysis is therefore shifted by the misspecification bias. With exact-balance weights, augmentation by an outcome model built from the balanced terms reproduces MAIC.
findings: Both models correct: augmented bias equal to the omitted-variable bias in all 16 scenarios; largest difference from correct outcome regression 0.0015.
Omitted variable absent, one model wrong: augmented estimator unbiased (second null control held); the wrong single-model estimator biased by up to 0.20.
Both models wrong: bias additive in misspecification and omitted-variable parts, largest interaction 0.008, within 3 MCSE in 16 of 16 scenarios.

Registered region-inclusion criterion not met as stated (0.888 against a 0.90 threshold) because the region omitted sampling error; the misspecified region was displaced by 0.195 to 0.201 at every omitted-variable strength.
not_answered: Continuous outcome only; no cross-fitting; drMAIC E-value screen and a formally bias-indexed doubly robust estimator not run. Peer review has not been done.
methods_compared: MAIC with correct or wrong weights
outcome regression with correct or wrong model
augmented (doubly robust) estimator under the four combinations
